findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The standing freezer in the kitchen has a large accumulation of ice observed. The PIC was shown and instructed to remove the ice. It is highly suggested that a pan be placed under the condenser unit so that the ice accumulation can be caught and the food packages protected from possible contaminants. Ensure that the ice is managed moving forward.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. 

A food employee was observed to wash their hands and then turn off the faucet with their bare hands. Education was conducted and the hands rewashed to correct. A paper towel was used the second time. Ensure a clean barrier is used to turn off the faucet during hand washing so as to prevent recontamination of the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani bucket in the kitchen is observed with a concentration of approximately 10 ppm CL. Effective levels per the bottle require approximately 150-200 ppm. A larger jug is made at the beginning of the day and dispensed into the buckets throughout the day. This jug is observed at the 200 ppm concentration. The bucket was remade during this inspection from the jug to correct the violation. The bucket should be replaced/remade prior to the concentration becoming too low to effectively sanitize food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
No certified food protection manager present at time of inspection. Main kitchen PIC is out today. Another employee is scheduled to complete the CFM course as well. Ensure sufficient staff are CFMs to cover all shifts of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Kitchen manager has an expired food manager certification and just took a course this week. Exam was completed on 2/27 and results have not yet been received. Manager will contact SCDPH with certification number and expiration date once she has results.  

Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Food employees were observed touching the handles of the manual faucet and paper towel dispenser without a barrier after handwashing process was completed. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. 
Proper handwashing technique poster was observed at handsink for reference.

To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink and handles of paper towel dispensers. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Spray bottle of bleach solution in one classroom was observed at ~100ppm. The label directions show a required concentration of 150-200ppm. Solution was discarded and new solution prepared at proper concentration of 200ppm. 

A chemical sanitizer shall be used in accordance with EPA-registered label use instructions. Maintain solutions at 150-200ppm per label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 A package of open deli ham was observed with a date mark of 2/11/19 in the cooler. Manager stated that was the day the product was received. Product was likely past the 7 day time frame for use and was discarded. Proper date marking of opened ready to eat TCS foods was discussed. 
Educational handout on date marking was provided.

Commercially processed, refrigerated, ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods (TCS) shall be clearly marked, at the time the original packaging is opened and if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12 Spray bottles of bleach solutions in three classrooms were observed at concentrations above 200ppm. Bleach strips were bleached out and began to turn white. Solutions were discarded and new solutions prepared at proper concentration.

Poisonous or toxic materials shall be used according to manufacturer's use directions included in labeling. Maintain bleach solutions at 150-200ppm as directed on label instructions, and use test strips to verify proper concentration.
